answer.rationale: Memory_73 explicitly warns against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable—the acquired cohort from exp_73 failed at renewal despite +18% qualified revenue gain and +31% signup. This directly contradicts leadership's instinct to match competitor pricing. Instead, deploy activation_messaging (memory_91: proven to improve week-one engagement and nudge accounts to first meaningful action) paired with simplified onboarding friction (memory_31, memory_86: +9% to +15% activation lift). This addresses the root problem—price-sensitive accounts churn because they perceive low value, not because price alone is uncompetitive. By accelerating time-to-value and deepening early engagement, we improve retention probability within the cohort most at risk. For enterprise accounts showing churn signals, parallel sales-assisted intervention (memory_44) is warranted but scaled carefully. Promotional pricing is explicitly contraindicated by our own data. This preserves long-term qualified revenue by solving for value realization rather than unsustainable discounting, and it buys time before next week's verification budget reopens.
